The only reason why it plays well is because it's 2026 and the level of cringe have shifted to a complete new horizons, which makes this story a walk in the park. But if you play this game with voicelines muted + no subtitles and make up your own story based on what's happening on the screen - it's not that bad! You basically saved the galaxy from super duper bad people that are totally not engaging in incestual activities by sucking each other throughout the whole storyline, surely not...

Moving onto another negative aspect, which would be level design. Placing the drop pod and galaxy map in two completely opposite corners of the Sanctuary III is crazy work, all because making a ladder downstairs would be impossible due to placement of pay to win diamond gamba room or whatever it is. Most of other location are also annoying to navigate, the minimap is a fever dream, the large area map would show as if there is no passage while in reality its just a cliff where you can jump off. You get used to it but holy lord, someone forgot a bag of shrooms at the kitchen in the map designer isle for sure. As always, guns guns guns, as in all BD series, they still cooking, HARD. Not sure about billion guns claims, since you anyways going to be dressed up in full legendaries with one-tap weapons before level 20 and have auto-sell enabled for anything below it, still, shooting is enjoyable and fun. [Purchased on sale September 2026]

If you're a fan of Borderlands you will feel right at home in Borderlands 3, and newcomers can expect an experience that is accessible and rewarding even without playing the previous titles. [Note for controller users: Adjust in-game dead zone settings if you are getting unintended joystick inputs, this fixed my issues using a Dual Sense controller]

When it wants to be, it's one of the most fun shooters around, especially with friends. When does it want to be? 'Bout twice an hour. Diverse build potential, really fun and cool guns, great movement. Everything else about this game? Utter garbage. 

The characters are bland and uninteresting. The story is far too long yet at the same time nearly devoid of anything noteworthy or fun whenever you are out of combat. And you're out of combat a LOT. Every single quest has at least two-thirds of its objectives such thrilling things like: "Follow," "talk to," "observe," "wait for," "go back to." God the amount of quests that boil down to "Go here, talk to this guy, listen to him talk for 90 seconds, go there, shoot some things along the way and start threatening to have a good time, follow this guy, talk to that guy, go back to sanctuary, talk to Lillith, go somewhere else, TALK TO A GUY AGAIN." It'd be better if literally anyone in this game had anything interesting to say, but they just yap and yap and say the most unfunny, millennial-ass, MCU-style reference humor for several minutes while the next objective hasn't even appeared on your map, so you can't even move and continue the game while you listen to them talk. You just have to fuckn stand there and listen. 

The writing is atrocious. Maybe once, ONCE every 400 jokes something will make you chuckle, but you feel bad about it. The game demands you care about its story, demands you get emotionally invested, but it's genuinely so bad and the dogshit melodrama completely falls flat. The writing team for this game needs to be flung into orbit.

Whenever you're in combat the game is fast and fun, but combat is so short and far, FAR too easy. There are two difficulty settings: "normal" and "easier." No hard mode at all. If you clear the main campaign, you get to do a kind of New Game+ which ups the difficulty, but demanding your players beat your fuckass story once before telling them to go through it AGAIN so they can actually have fun this time is insane.

While the gameplay itself is pretty fun, never in my life have I played a game with writing/dialogue so bad that it made me cringe and want to give up halfway through. The new characters are also pretty obnoxious. It's a shame. Borderlands 2 and tales from the borderlands were fun games. This one just makes you wonder how stoned the people who made it were at the time.

Six years later I decided to review this game. Why? Well, because every time I think of the COVID-19 pandemic, I think of this game. It was released in March 2020; the very beginning of quarantine when everyone panicked and closed their doors to remain inside for weeks on end. I was in college at the time and we got sent home to complete classes online for the remainder of the spring semester. While I understand the pandemic was a terrifying experience for some to say the least, I can also respect everyone's unique experiences with it. For me personally, it was a time of bliss and fond memories. Every morning I would wake up, workout, go to my online classes, and play this game for the remainder of the day until three in the morning with my friends. That was practically all of our schedules for weeks on end as there were no outside commitments holding us back. It was awesome. The story of Borderlands 3 is honestly ass and I can barely remember any of it even after watching a story summary video. What I do remember though is the awesome typical gameplay loop of Borderlands as a “looter shooter”. At first I thought the characters you can play as were kinda lame, but they grew on me and became some of my favorites in the series. 

Borderlands 3 is also the only game I can think of where I stopped playing because it was so easy that it was not fun anymore. Sometime soon after the launch, there was an event that boosted drop rates of all legendary weapons and equipment. I tried to look through the game's updates and news to find when it occurred or what it was called, but had no luck. Since my friends and I were playing practically 24/7 due to the COVID lockdown, we basically got every legendary weapon in the game including their different elemental variants in a matter of days, maybe even hours. However, there was no better weapon than The Lob: a rifle that shot a slow travelling elemental orb, killing any enemy instantly and shredding bosses like melted butter. All of our weapon slots were just different elemental variants of The Lob. Once the first DLC rolled around, we started the first mission and quit after an hour in because it wasn't a challenge at all. I'm not joking when I say everything would die in one hit with the lob and it required ZERO brain power to use. 

Since then, my friends and I never returned to the game. Does that mean the game was bad? Not at all. I think we had a blast with it for what it was, though we never did get to experience the later DLC’s. Maybe it's time to travel back to experience those new additions and find the new broken gun. I haven't touched Borderlands 4 and probably won't until all the DLC has been released in a package at a discounted price similar to the Handsome Jack collection of the past. From what I have heard though it is more of the same with a slightly improved story. While Borderlands 3 is a great looter-shooter with improvements to gameplay mechanics and other systems, I don't think it beat’s Borderlands 2.

Borderlands 3 : A Loot-Shooter With No Story to Loot

Borderlands 3 is a game that somehow manages to have more guns than good dialogue, which is genuinely impressive when you consider how much dialogue there is.

On paper, Borderlands 3 should be fantastic. You have guns lots of guns. You have ridiculous enemies, colourful environments, explosions, skill trees, and enough loot to make your inventory look like the aftermath of a particularly violent yard sale.

And yet, somehow, the biggest thing I wanted to shoot by the end wasn't an enemy.

It was the skip cutscene button.

The Story Is Absolutely Painful
Let's address the biggest problem first: the story is awful.

The Calypso Twins are presented as these terrifying new villains, but instead of feeling like intimidating threats, they often feel like two obnoxious YouTubers who somehow gained access to a galactic broadcasting network.

Troy and Tyreen spend an enormous amount of time talking at you, shouting at you, livestreaming their villainy and generally making you wish your Vault Hunter could simply walk over and unplug their router.

The problem isn't that Borderlands has never been funny. The previous games were full of ridiculous characters and stupid jokes, but they generally understood that comedy works better when you aren't constantly screaming "LOOK! THIS IS THE JOKE!" directly into the player's face.

Borderlands 3 frequently feels like it has mistaken being loud for being funny.

And then there's the fact that the story constantly wants you to care about characters while simultaneously doing everything possible to make you care less.

The Characters: Please Stop Talking
The Vault Hunters are supposed to be the stars of the show, yet they frequently feel like they're standing in the corner of their own game.

This is especially frustrating because Amara is actually fun to play.

Amara feels powerful, satisfying and properly suited to the chaos of Borderlands. Her abilities make you feel like you're playing a ridiculous space-powered badass rather than someone who accidentally wandered into a firefight carrying a slightly better assault rifle.

The other characters, however, just didn't click with me.

Moze has a cool concept with Iron Bear, but the character can often feel like you're playing Iron Bear: The Occasional Human. There's plenty of potential there, but I never found her gameplay loop as satisfying as Amara's.

FL4K is probably the most interesting conceptually, especially with the pets, but the gameplay never quite gave me the same feeling of controlled chaos that Amara did.

And Zane...

Zane feels like Borderlands 3 looked at every possible character gimmick, threw them into a blender, and said, "Sure, that'll do."

Obviously, character preference is subjective, and different builds can completely change how each Vault Hunter feels. But for me, Amara was the only one who consistently made me think, "Yes. This is exactly how I want to play this game."

The Weirdest Part: The Game Is Still Fun
And this is where Borderlands 3 becomes difficult to review.

Because despite all of that...

It's still incredibly fun to shoot things.

The gunplay is excellent. Weapons feel satisfying, enemies explode in increasingly ridiculous ways, and there is always another piece of loot waiting around the corner.

Borderlands 3 understands the ancient gamer instinct:

"I don't need this gun, but what if the next gun is slightly better?"

So you pick it up.

Then another one drops.

Then another.

Three hours later you're standing in Sanctuary staring at your inventory wondering why you have 47 guns when you only actually use three.

The gameplay loop is basically digital hoarding with explosions.

And annoyingly, it works.

The Real Villain Is the Dialogue
Every time the gameplay starts getting really good, the game seems to remember:

"Oh shit. We wrote a story."

And suddenly you're standing there listening to another conversation while your character stares blankly into the middle distance.

It's especially frustrating because the environments, shooting and loot systems are good enough to carry the game almost entirely by themselves.

I don't need a cinematic masterpiece.

I just need the game to stop interrupting me every five minutes to explain why I should care about someone I've already forgotten.

Final Verdict
Borderlands 3 is like ordering an enormous pizza and discovering that the toppings are fantastic but someone has replaced the cheese with a three-hour podcast.

The gunplay is great, the loot system is addictive, the environments are colourful and chaotic, and Amara is an absolute blast to play.

But the story is a slog, the villains are irritating rather than intimidating, and several of the playable characters never reached the same level of enjoyment for me that Amara did.

It's a bizarre game because the moment-to-moment gameplay can have you thinking:

"This is awesome."

Then a character starts talking.

And you're thinking:

"This is not awesome."

Then you get a legendary gun.

"THIS IS AWESOME AGAIN."

Then someone starts talking.

"PLEASE GOD, NO."

Borderlands 3 ultimately feels like a fantastic loot-shooter trapped inside a story it desperately wishes you would pay attention to.

Great guns. Great shooting. Great loot. Terrible story.

And if I could give the narrative a legendary drop rate, I'd make it 0.0001%.

PROS:

- Nice graphics.
- Great voice acting.
- Fine music
- Fine combat

CONS:

- The sanctuary ship is an utter mess to navigate. Everything is at the far end of everything, forcing you to go back and forth long distances to get things done. The ship itself is impressive and nice-looking, but the minimap is almost useless when navigating it.

- The main villains of this story are insufferable and badly written

- Side quests are boring and feel unrewarding. You level up and gain loot faster simply by playing the main story. The side quests do not offer any meaningful value loot, exp, or story-wise.

- You can accidently sell your equipped weapons at a shop without any warning.

- The quest markers often feel misleading or very badly placed. It can be hard to make out where to go sometimes.

- Movement feels far too simplistic (Borderlands 4 fixed this)

- Quest log doesn't show enough information where the quest takes place exactly if different from your current location.

- Sometimes you can feel that the game is bugged when it's just bad quest design.
